newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM approves aluminium warehouses, trade members.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM approves aluminium warehouses, trade members.

text.p: The Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) board of directors approved 16 warehouse locations throughout Japan and 74 trading members for its aluminium futures contract due to begin trading in April, a TOCOM spokesman said on Thursday.
The trading members include all nine of Japan's leading trade houses, as well as Engelhard Metals Japan Ltd, a subsidiary of U.S.-based Engelhard Corp.
The exchange has also given final approval to recommendations issued last August regarding commissions, margins and daily trading limits, the spokesman said.

Regular commissions were set at 6,000 yen per contract, although commissions for members and registered hedgers will be a much lower 1,000 yen. Large orders will be extended a 30 percent discount on that portion of the order exceeding 1,000 lots. One lot equals 10 tonnes.
Initial margins were set at 60,000 yen at aluminium prices of 149 yen per kg or less, 75,000 yen at prices of 150 to 199 yen, 90,000 yen at 200 to 249 yen and 105,000 yen at 250 yen or more.
